reportName: Learning Local Demo Auth Persistence Security Gate Matrix

currentStatus.summary: Prisma auth persistence code, schema, migration, fail-closed behavior, two-client revocation, rollback, and forward repair are disposable-local verified while production readiness remains false.
remainingLocalDemoNotes: The Prisma session and shared auth operational-control providers are implemented but not production-enabled; approved staging rehearsal, dashboards, alert routing, retention ownership, and manual go-live approval remain open.
Security review, staging backup/restore rehearsal, migration approval, retention approval, and manual go-live approval remain required before production enablement.

securityGateRows.contractSurface: AuthSessionStore production repository contract for auth_sessions, auth_refresh_tokens, and auth_session_audit_events.
securityGateRows.expectedProductionContract: A future PostgreSQL/Prisma repository must implement the existing AuthSessionStore methods with atomic writes for session state, refresh-token state, and append-only audit events.
securityGateRows.localFixtureEvidence: AUTH_SESSION_STORE now selects FixtureBackedAuthSessionStore for local demo or PrismaAuthSessionStore for explicit disposable local/staging use; the migration and repository contract pass against a random localhost database.
requiredProductionControls: Store only refresh-token hashes, never raw refresh tokens.
Use indexed session id, user id, device id, state, and expiresAt columns.
Constrain refresh-token state transitions to ACTIVE, ROTATED, REUSED, REVOKED, and EXPIRED.
Write audit events append-only with admin/support read filters.
plannedVerification: Repository contract and migration/rollback tests pass against a disposable non-production database.
Staging migration diff, backup/restore, and security review remain required before any production deploy.
securityGateRows.rollbackOrMigrationNote: Add tables behind a repository provider flag; rollback before production writes may drop tables, while rollback after writes must disable the provider and preserve data for audit.
securityGateRows.evidenceSummary: Production schema/repository design is documented as a contract only; no production DB was read or mutated.

securityGateRows.contractSurface: Cross-instance session and refresh-token revocation behavior for JWT guard and refresh endpoint.
securityGateRows.expectedProductionContract: Every API instance must deny a session after the central repository marks it ENDED, REVOKED, or EXPIRED; cache invalidation must be bounded by a documented max staleness window.
securityGateRows.localFixtureEvidence: Job 00059 uses two independent Prisma clients against one disposable localhost database; revocation by instance A is denied by instance B.
requiredProductionControls: Central revocation version or updatedAt cursor checked by every instance.
Refresh-token reuse revokes the related session family across devices.
JWT guard must fail closed when repository lookup or revocation cache is unavailable.
plannedVerification: Two-instance non-production smoke: revoke on instance A and deny on instance B.
Cache outage test proves fail-closed behavior for protected routes.
securityGateRows.rollbackOrMigrationNote: Distributed revocation must launch with a kill switch that reverts traffic to the current local/session guard behavior only in non-production until manual approval.
securityGateRows.evidenceSummary: Distributed revocation is specified as an expected cross-instance contract and remains a production blocker until staged.

securityGateRows.contractSurface: Refresh-token retention, rotation, reuse response, and session-family revocation policy.
securityGateRows.expectedProductionContract: Rotated, reused, revoked, and expired refresh-token hashes must be retained long enough for replay detection and audit while raw token values remain unavailable.
securityGateRows.localFixtureEvidence: Job 00037 refresh lifecycle matrix covers rotation denial, reuse denial, session revocation, and audit visibility with fixture rows.
requiredProductionControls: Retain inactive refresh-token hashes for at least 30 days, subject to legal/security review.
On reused token detection, mark token REUSED, revoke the session family, and emit an audit event.
Deny refresh for expired or non-active tokens with a stable unauthorized response.
plannedVerification: Retention cleanup dry-run report shows deleted candidates without deleting production data.
Replay test proves reused token denial and session-family revocation.
securityGateRows.rollbackOrMigrationNote: Retention cleanup must run in dry-run mode first; rollback disables cleanup scheduling and preserves token hash rows.
securityGateRows.evidenceSummary: Refresh-token retention and reuse response are policy evidence only; no production token data was accessed.

securityGateRows.contractSurface: Auth lifecycle audit retention, admin/support visibility, and read-only export policy.
securityGateRows.expectedProductionContract: Session and refresh-token lifecycle audit events must be append-only, retained according to policy, and exportable through a redacted read-only admin/support path.
securityGateRows.localFixtureEvidence: Fixture audit events are visible to ADMIN and SUPPORT roles while learner roles receive no audit rows.
requiredProductionControls: Audit export must be read-only and scoped to admin/support roles.
Exports must redact token hashes and avoid raw IP/user-agent payloads unless approved.
Retention must be documented before production enablement.
plannedVerification: Read-only export smoke proves admin/support can export and student cannot.
Audit payload scan proves no raw refresh tokens or secrets are present.
securityGateRows.rollbackOrMigrationNote: Audit tables are append-only; rollback may disable export endpoints but must not delete retained audit rows.
securityGateRows.evidenceSummary: Audit retention/export policy is represented as read-only fixture evidence and remains production gated.

securityGateRows.contractSurface: Login, refresh, logout, session revocation, audit export, and cleanup monitoring hooks.
securityGateRows.expectedProductionContract: Auth endpoints must emit rate-limit decisions and monitoring counters for success, denial, reuse detection, cleanup, repository errors, and audit export reads.
securityGateRows.localFixtureEvidence: AUTH_OPERATIONAL_CONTROL now provides deterministic hashed-key login/refresh throttling and counters for success, denial, replay, cleanup, repository errors, and audit export without installing a live monitoring provider.
requiredProductionControls: Replace the process-local fixture with a shared multi-instance limiter keyed by approved actor, IP, and device signals.
Export the implemented counters through an approved metrics adapter and retention policy.
Route alerts for refresh-token replay spikes and repository lookup failures to an acknowledged incident owner.
plannedVerification: Completed locally: deterministic tests verify counter names, hashed-key snapshots, and role-scoped audit export totals.
Completed locally: repeated login and refresh failures return 429; rate-limit seam outage returns service unavailable.
Still required: multi-process staging smoke proves shared windows, metric export, and alert routing.
securityGateRows.rollbackOrMigrationNote: Monitoring hooks must be additive; rollback removes dashboards/alerts before removing emitted metric names.
securityGateRows.evidenceSummary: Rate-limit and monitoring hooks are implemented and fixture-verified without calling any live provider or exposing secrets; shared production controls remain blocked.

securityGateRows.contractSurface: Auth persistence migration, rollback, and production enablement runbook notes.
securityGateRows.expectedProductionContract: Production auth persistence must ship through staged migrations, feature flags, backup verification, and a rollback plan that preserves security audit data.
securityGateRows.localFixtureEvidence: This local-demo matrix records the migration/rollback requirements before any schema migration is created.
requiredProductionControls: Run migration in staging with disposable fixtures before production.
Take and verify backup/restore evidence before enabling persistent auth sessions.
Keep production_ready=false until security review and manual go-live approval.
plannedVerification: Staging migration dry-run and rollback rehearsal evidence.
Backup/restore rehearsal evidence tied to auth session tables.
securityGateRows.rollbackOrMigrationNote: Rollback after production writes must disable new writes and preserve tables; destructive rollback is allowed only before production enablement.
securityGateRows.evidenceSummary: Rollback and migration notes are captured as local evidence; no deploy or production migration was run.
